title: Task host
description: startTask() shows one blocking overlay for a job the user must wait for: label, current step, progress, elapsed time and an optional Cancel. Mount TaskHost once in the root layout, next to ToastHost and ConfirmHost.
when: The user started a job and cannot do anything useful until it finishes: an upload before printing, an import, a firmware update, a payment step, an AI job that the next screen needs.

instead.need: Work the user can keep going during (a background sync, an export)
instead.use: Progress inline, or toast() when it ends

instead.need: A page or section waiting for its data
A button running its own short action

a11y: An alertdialog named by the label, aria-busy while it runs; label and step sit in a polite live region, the elapsed time is not announced.
Focus stays inside (on Cancel when there is one); Escape and Cancel only exist when onCancel is set.

examples.title: No Cancel, ends with fail()
examples.description: fail() closes the overlay and shows a danger toast.

notes: <TaskHost /> goes once in the root layout (see Theme › Root layout); startTask() works from any event handler.
One task at a time: startTask() while one runs replaces it, and the old handle does nothing. update({ value }) takes 0–100; leave value out for an indeterminate bar.
Cancel and Escape close the overlay first, then call onCancel: stop the job there.
